also: take as much as you like

terms.gloss: take as much as you like
evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.7.16: at tū, quantum vīs, tolle
terms.comment: The host’s words in Horace, pressing pears on a guest who says he has had enough. Tollere is to take something up from where it lies; sūmere is to take food for oneself.

evidence: Petr. 34.1: sī quis nostrum iterum vellet mulsum sūmere

phrases.latin: Vēscere, sōdēs. — Jam satis est. — At tū, quantum vīs, tolle. — Benignē.
phrases.english: Do eat, please. — I’ve had enough. — Well, take as much as you like. — No, thank you.

phrases.latin: nōn est quod timeās, ait; et, quae dēbētur pars tuae modestiae, audācter tolle
phrases.english: “There is nothing to fear,” he said, “and take boldly the share your modesty has earned.”
Take as much as you like; there’s plenty left.

sources: Lewis & Short: tollo · Lewis & Short: sumo
